mechanism: Decode every JSON object into an ordered raw key/value pair frame rather than an ordinary dict; recursively scan child frames while retaining the parent pair frame; within each frame normalize keys to NFC and record collisions without throwing; only permit ordinary dict materialization for a frame after its own collision scan is clean.
tested_scope: Exactly one fixed-source deterministic local control. It verifies only frame-local NFC collision detection before ordinary dict materialization, first-sibling isolation, and continued traversal of the outer parent pair frame after the second-sibling collision is recorded. It does not prove arbitrary Unicode equivalence classes, streaming parser restart, hostile-size bounds, or global scheduled-Chat parity.
observation: The first sibling frame was clean. The second sibling frame independently detected the NFC-equivalent raw keys é and é. Because collisions were recorded rather than raised and the parent was retained as a raw pair frame, the outer parent remained traversable and subsequently detected its own separate NFC collision. Frame-local collision state did not leak from the first sibling into the second sibling or from the second sibling into the parent.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to this one fixed-source local frame-isolation control. Do not generalize to full parser safety, persistence safety, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and required persisted/read-back preflight, execute exactly one deterministic recurrence-sensitive reconstruction control using the same raw-pair-frame scanner state representation: serialize a checkpoint immediately after the second-sibling frame has recorded its NFC collision but before the outer parent frame is scanned, reconstruct from that checkpoint in a fresh local state, and determine only whether the resumed scan produces the same outer-parent collision exactly once with no duplicate second-sibling event. Do not test a second case.
